query: Our LTV:CAC is 4:1 so the economics look great and I want to pour money into paid ads to grow faster. CAC is 1200, customers pay 100/month, and gross margin is around 75%. Should we scale spend?
expected_behavior: Refuses to bless scaling on the 4:1 ratio alone and computes CAC payback in months (1200 / (100 x 0.75) = 16 months), calling out that a long payback is a cash-flow risk even with a healthy ratio
Insists LTV:CAC be reported as a triplet with payback and the churn assumption behind LTV, and notes the ratio is meaningless without the churn rate that drives LTV
Checks that LTV and contribution margin are computed on gross margin, not revenue, so the unit is not secretly negative
Recommends measuring retention and CAC by cohort rather than a blended average before increasing spend
Warns that scaling spend on a 16-month payback will starve cash and suggests levers (faster payback, annual prepay, cheaper channels) instead of an immediate budget increase
